 Jason Derulo to Headline Entertainment Lineup at Qatar Grand Prix Weekend
 by 
 Speedway Digest Staff 
 November 17, 2026 
Reading Time: 3 mins read
 0 Qatar Grand Prix Graphic
 DOHA, Qatar — The Formula 1 Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix is adding another global star to its race weekend festivities, with multi-platinum recording artist Jason Derulo set to headline the post-race concert at Lusail International Circuit.
 Event organizers announced Derulo will perform on Sunday, Nov. 29, following the conclusion of the Formula 1 season’s penultimate race weekend, adding a major entertainment attraction to an event that continues to position itself as one of Formula 1’s premier destination races.
 The performance will take place on the Lusail Live stage and is included with all three-day race tickets.
 Derulo arrives in Qatar as one of the most recognizable figures in contemporary pop music. The singer, songwriter and performer has sold more than 250 million singles worldwide and amassed a global following exceeding 300 million across social media platforms.

 His catalog includes chart-topping hits such as “Whatcha Say” and “Savage Love,” while his latest collaboration, “Mi Chico” with Melody and DJ Goja, became one of the year’s biggest international successes. The track spent six weeks atop Billboard’s U.S. Afrobeats chart, generated hundreds of millions of streams and inspired a viral dance trend that accumulated more than 2 billion views worldwide.
 The appearance comes as Derulo prepares for the release of his upcoming album, The Last Dance (Part 2) , scheduled for early 2027.
 For Formula 1 fans, the concert caps a packed Sunday schedule that begins with the FIA Formula 2 Feature Race and the traditional Formula 1 Drivers’ Parade before the main event under the lights at Lusail International Circuit.
 The addition of Derulo continues Formula 1’s broader strategy of pairing world-class entertainment with Grand Prix weekends. Similar entertainment programs have become staples of marquee races in Las Vegas, Abu Dhabi, Singapore and Miami, helping transform race weekends into multi-day entertainment festivals.
 Qatar’s event has increasingly embraced that model since joining the Formula 1 calendar, combining elite motorsport with concerts, hospitality experiences and fan activations.
 Demand appears strong for the 2026 edition. Organizers reported that several premium hospitality offerings, including Novikov at Premiere Hospitality and the Lusail Hill Lounge, have already sold out. The F1 Experiences Champions Club remains available for fans seeking premium access during the weekend.
 Grandstand and general admission packages remain available, with ticket options ranging from Lusail Hill general admission to premium seating around the circuit. Organizers are also offering discounted pricing for university students and senior citizens.
 With the Formula 1 championship entering its closing stages and one of pop music’s biggest performers scheduled to take the stage after the checkered flag, the Qatar Grand Prix is positioning itself as one of the season’s most significant sporting and entertainment events.
